note:
#4497 is a CODE-QUALITY issue, not a correctness one: both spellings in repro.hlsl compile cleanly and produce valid DXIL, and every probe -- reproducing or not -- exits 0. So the predicate is structural, over the disassembly, and nothing about it keys on exit status or diagnostics.

Reported symptom (issue body, 2022-06-02): when the StructuredBuffer element is passed BY VALUE into fct1(SData), the float load of SData::value is emitted UNCONDITIONALLY in the entry block and the two [branch] ifs are flattened into a single branch; when the buffer is indexed directly (fct2/test2) that same load is sunk into the block guarded by 'type == 0'. The reporter's ask is the load, not the branch: 'the memory fetch is done only when the fi[r]st condition is true'.

Clause 4 IS the symptom, expressed as a position rather than as text: starting at the entry function's 'define', reach a dx.op.bufferLoad.f32 / dx.op.rawBufferLoad.f32 call WITHOUT crossing a 'br i1'. That is exactly 'the float load is in the entry block, so it runs whatever the value of .type'. Predicates run under re.MULTILINE and not DOTALL, so the cross-line scan is written [\s\S] rather than '.'.

Why '(?:raw)?[bB]ufferLoad': a StructuredBuffer element load lowers to dx.op.bufferLoad (opcode 68) at SM 6.0/6.1 and to dx.op.rawBufferLoad (opcode 139) at SM 6.2 and above -- the latter is what the reporter's own quoted IR shows. Both spellings are matched so the same predicate scores every release and every profile variant. The optional 'raw' group is not cosmetic: the first version of this predicate wrote '@dx\.op\.[bB]ufferLoad', which cannot match '@dx.op.rawBufferLoad' because 'raw' sits between the prefix and the capital B. It scored the ps_6_0 primary as a reproduction and BOTH SM 6.2+ identity controls as clean -- i.e. it would have reported the maintainer's own published ps_6_6 configuration as fixed. Only --expect match on those controls caught it. The entry function is named '@test1' here, NOT '@main' (dxc keeps -E's name in the DXIL), so the anchor accepts any name.

Clause 4 is position-shaped, i.e. partly an ABSENCE ('no br i1 before'), and SKILL step 6 warns that an absence is satisfied for free by a compile that never got started. Clauses 1-3 are the anti-vacuity anchors, and each rules out a specific way of matching for the wrong reason:
  1. dx.op.discard proves codegen ran to completion and emitted the body of fct1/fct2 -- a release that rejected the input or died early cannot satisfy it.
  2. a separate integer load proves .type is still loaded on its own, so 'nothing was sunk' cannot be satisfied by a build that merged both fields into one wide load (in which case there is no separable load to sink, and that would be a different observation deserving a look rather than a silent 'repro').
  3. at least one 'br i1' proves the shader was not flattened to straight-line code altogether -- if the compiler ever discharged the branches entirely, clause 4 would be true for a reason that has nothing to do with the issue.

CONTROLS (all captured, all with --expect, all against this same predicate):
  variant-test2-direct-*.txt    -T ps_6_0 -E test2  --expect no-match  -- THE control. Same file, same profile, one flag different: the direct-indexing form the reporter says is better. Its float load sits after 'br i1', so clause 4 fails. This is what proves the predicate discriminates rather than firing on any shader containing a buffer load.
  variant-test2-direct-ps66-*   -T ps_6_6 -E test2  --expect no-match  -- the same contrast at the maintainer's published profile.
  variant-asfiled-ps66-*        -T ps_6_6 -E test1  --expect match     -- identity control for cmd.txt's profile change (see cmd-as-filed.txt).
  variant-ps62-*                -T ps_6_2 -E test1  --expect match     -- identity control at the SM where the load lowers to rawBufferLoad, matching the reporter's quoted IR.

Deliberately NOT in the predicate: the 'and i1' that flattens the two conditions, the !dx.controlflow.hints metadata, SSA register numbers, and !dbg/llvm.dbg.value (the reporter compiled with -Zi, from a larger private shader; their IR carries storeOutput calls and mangled ps_test1/ps_test2 names that the public snippet cannot reproduce). Those are instance details of one report, and old releases print IR differently.
